research_brief.topic: How a Solo Founder Turned Support Tickets Into a Product Roadmap
research_brief.source_summary: A synthetic founder story about using repeated customer support pain to guide roadmap priorities.
source_boundaries: The founder, company, customers, and support details are fictional.
The only supported lesson is that repeated support patterns can inform product priorities.
open_questions: No real product category, customer segment, or measurable result is provided.
do_not_claim: Do not imply the workflow is proven by external data.

claim_registry.claim: Repeated support tickets can reveal product roadmap priorities.
claim_registry.supporting_source: Fixture source notes describe repeated customer pain as the core lesson.
Fixture source notes explicitly prohibit real customers and proprietary support details.

narrative_strategy.core_angle: The roadmap became clearer when the founder stopped treating support as noise and started looking for repeated pain.
narrative_strategy.audience_promise: A practical operating lesson for founders and product teams.
narrative_strategy.emotional_arc: Overwhelmed by tickets, then focused by patterns, then resolved around a clearer priority.
narrative_strategy.hook_strategy: Lead with the counterintuitive idea that the roadmap was already in the inbox.
narrative_strategy.ending_strategy: Close on support as a place where priorities become visible.
narrative_strategy.visual_strategy: Use a consistent founder workspace, anonymized ticket cards, note clustering, and roadmap sketches without readable UI text.
narrative_strategy.voice_strategy: Grounded founder voice, calm and credible, with clean narration and no provider-specific emotion tags.
narrative_strategy.music_strategy: Warm minimal piano or soft pulse that supports reflection without drama.

hook_options: The roadmap was hiding in the same customer complaint, repeated again and again.
I stopped guessing what to build when I reread the support inbox.
One founder habit changed the roadmap: tagging every repeated pain.
clean_script.selected_hook: The roadmap was hiding in the same customer complaint, repeated again and again.
clean_script.narration_script: The roadmap was hiding in the same customer complaint, repeated again and again. At first, every support ticket felt like a distraction from building. Then patterns started to show up. Different customers were asking for the same fix in different words. Instead of adding another idea to a wish list, the founder grouped the pain, sketched the workflow, and turned the loudest pattern into the next release. Support is not just where problems arrive. It is where priorities become visible.
